title: 8-round AES-192 value-constraint DS-MITM, practical-data tradeoff endpoint

target.description: 8-round AES-192, with initial K^0 whitening and the source's equivalent-key/inverse-MixColumns representation. Section 2 defines the final round without MixColumns. The procedure includes full master-key reconstruction and testing.

setting.key_relation: One unknown AES master key; standard key schedule is used to join partial round-key guesses.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: 2^40 chosen plaintexts in structures of 2^32 texts varying diagonal D3, with the other bytes fixed per structure
assumptions: 2^8 structures of 2^32 chosen plaintexts, four fixed-byte value constraints, nested MITM online and offline phases.

Section 4.4 normalizes r-round encryption computation by 16r S-box evaluations, excluding key-schedule S-boxes from that baseline. Memory accesses to non-small/huge tables remain a separate cost coordinate.
The 28-byte filter leaves an expected 2^112 candidates; the remaining six bytes are searched at up to 2^48 encryptions each, contributing about 2^160 encryptions.
Candidate counts and matching costs use the author's average-case model; a whole-attack numerical success probability is not reported.

field_conflicts.label: Missing fixed key-schedule constant
field_conflicts.description: The printed K0[12] identity omits Rcon4=08 under the standard AES schedule. Its RHS is K0[12] xor08, while the adjacent K5(AES192)/K1(AES256) relation is retained. This is a local known additive constant, not a new search exponent or a K0/K1 relabelling. Source costs are unchanged.
